While he kept it roasting as if devoid of sensation, the king, astounded by his strange conduct, sprang from his seat and ordered the youth to be removed from the altar. Go, he said, you have been a worse enemy to yourself than to me. I would invoke blessings on your courage if it were displayed for my country's sake as it is. I send you away exempt from all rights of war unheers and safe.

The Romans are crazy, demonic. None of this is true; it can't possibly be. You can’t put your hand in fire without feeling pain. But the Romans are taking proto-Indo-European myth and adapting it to their own history. Everything we've read is not true but the Romans believed it was.

So the story of Lucius Buddhist kicking out the Tarkkins is the story of the third man stealing a throne from Tarquin, and the story of the man sacrificing his twin is the story of Romulus and Remus. The most famous Roman ethics, called the Aeneid, at this time Augustus Caesar has a problem: everyone acknowledges Greek culture as superior due to Homer and the Iliad.

The Iliad ends with love and forgiveness, Achilles feeling guilt for killing Hector, and Priam forgiving him by kissing his hand. In this scene, Achilles sees Priam as his father, and they hug and weep together. This idea of love as a unifying force becomes the basis of Greek culture.

For the Romans, if you're a culture based on hate, love is the greatest enemy. Augustus Caesar will ask Virgil to rewrite this story in a way that puts hate at the center of the universe instead of love. The Aeneid by Virgil, considered one of the greatest books in human history, is propaganda. Virgil, being ordered by Augustus Caesar, writes it with each draft read and reworked by Augustus until he asks for the book to be burned before his death because using a poet's gift to promote hatred will send him to hell.

The Greeks have broken into Troy and are killing everyone. The son of Achilles named Pyrus is killing the sons of Priam, and Priam faces Pyrus, telling him: "You're the son of Achilles."
